searchText: Hi, is the p2p protocol used by Consensus layers the same with the on used with EL (apart from the different messages)? if yes, why does one start with enode: and the other with enr? No. Consensus uses libp2p but that’s not where the enrs come from - lib p2p primarily uses multiaddrs. It’s discv5 that uses enrs. So is that the same, EL uses libp2p too But one uses discv5 pretty sure EL uses devp2p Aaah Okay For discovery, all ELs should be using discv4 afaik uhg okay ELs are a bit more complex. They do use devp2p for actual peer connections but discovery is a mix of discv4, some dns based discovery and there is an off by default discv5 implementation in geth I think. do prysm have this logic packaged out somewhere? Under the hood, we use geth's implementation: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/master/p2p/discover/v5_udp.go ok nice, that is a dead end for me, thank you anyway <@687974325072035882> maybe I can help with your question? Well I want to try to connect to the CL p2p network And make a CL lightclient But first off I need the p2p layer, which I may implement by myself Since you need to connect to the CL P2P network, this might help you: https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/beacon-chain/p2p/service.go#L172
